items.title: Rajani Associates advises Modepro on acquisition by Refex
items.summary: Refex Life Sciences Private Limited has acquired 100% of Modepro India Private Limited, transitioning the entity from its founding promoters (the Kavalam family) to the new corporate management. Rajani Associates advised Modepro and its promoters, the Kavalam family, on this acquisition. The Firm's role included legal diligence handholding and advising clients on routine housekeeping and legal issues immerging out of the diligence exercise; advising clients on the hiving-off of certain identified assets of the Target Company; advising clients on the MIDC Agreements and their approvals; and preparing, negotiating, and finalizing the transaction and ancillary documents. The transaction team consisted of Amish Shroff (Partner), Karen Issac (Principal Associate) and Ruchi Sethna (Senior Associate). Modepro Modepro India Private Limited is a pharmaceutical company specializing in the manufacture of advanced intermediates for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and fine chemicals. items.title: IC RegFin Legal expands New Delhi presence with move to larger office
items.summary: IC RegFin Legal has announced the opening of its new three-storey office building, “RegFin House” in South Extension, New Delhi, marking a significant expansion of its presence in the capital. Designed to accommodate up to 100 professionals, the new office provides the capacity and infrastructure to support the continued growth of the firm's New Delhi practice and its wider pan-India expansion. The new office offers a contemporary, modern and thoughtfully designed workplace surrounded by greenery. The premises feature spacious work areas, multiple meeting rooms, a garden, a large cafeteria and a terrace overlooking a historical monument. The enhanced infrastructure has been designed to support the firm’s growing team and operations, while also providing substantial spaces for collaboration, team gatherings, client engagements and larger firm events. Speaking on the development, Tejesh Chitlangi , Managing Partner, IC RegFin Legal, said, “Our move to a larger New Delhi office reflects the growth trajectory of the firm and our confidence in the opportunities ahead. items.title: Vizag: Six-yr-old school kid collapses and dies soon after being slapped by teacher
items.summary: A six-year-old boy, Pranay Tej, died after collapsing in a classroom, soon after a teacher scolded and slapped him. The incident, captured on CCTV, happened on August 20 at the Little Garden School in Visakhapatnam, where Pranay was a UKG student. The visuals show the boy sitting on a bench across from the teacher, seeming distressed and asking not to be called to the front. When he went to the teacher apparently without having done some assigned work on his slate, she was seen shaking the boy and trying to unbutton his shirt. She then slapped him, and within seconds, he collapsed onto her. The child was taken to the King George Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The exact cause of his death is yet to be confirmed through a post-mortem examination. Pranay’s mother Sai Lakshmi told the media that her son said he was scared before leaving for school in the morning, saying his teacher might hit him for not doing his homework. “The teacher tried to strip him and hit him for not doing some work. items.title: JGU sets up Chief Justices of India Museum
items.summary: OP Jindal Global University (JGU) has set up a Chief Justices of India Museum on its campus in Sonipat, dedicated to the lives and legacies of those who have helmed the Supreme Court of India. Vice Chancellor (VC) Prof (Dr) C Raj Kumar said, "It is first of its kind, not only in India but, to the best of our knowledge, anywhere in the world." He added that the museum builds on JGU's Constitution Museum and that together, the two initiatives create a space to understand the constitutional and judicial journey of the country. Chief Justices of India Museum, OP Jindal Global University An introductory note issued by the University said that the museum extends the Constitution's vision of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity by focusing on the Supreme Court's role in giving those ideals life through its jurisprudence, institutional leadership and commitment to constitutional governance. Chief Justices of India Museum, OP Jindal Global University Through judicial archives, landmark judgments, personal memorabilia, photographs, multimedia installations and stories of judicial courage, the museum aims to make this journey accessible to scholars, students and citizens alike. items.title: College won’t lose Malayalam minority status merely because Nairs dominate management: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently refused to cancel the Malayalam linguistic minority status of Sree Ayyappa College for Women in Nagercoil over allegations that members of the Nair community dominated its management [Srinivasa Menon Vs State of Tamil Nadu]. A Bench of Justices CV Karthikeyan and R Sakthivel held that even if the institution’s present office-bearers were predominantly Nairs, that by itself would not affect its minority status so long as they were Malayalees and did not act against the interests of the Malayalam-speaking linguistic minority in Tamil Nadu. The judgment was delivered on August 18 while dismissing a public interest litigation filed by S Srinivasan Menon, founder trustee of Devi Seva Sangam. Menon had sought cancellation of the linguistic minority status of the college and the Sree Ayyappa College Educational Society, which runs it. The college was granted Malayalam linguistic minority status in 1987 and receives financial aid from the Tamil Nadu government. items.title: Koodathayi case: Ernakulam court injuncts web series 'Anali' from identifying Jolly Joseph as lead accused
items.summary: A munsiff court in Kerala's Ernakulam has passed an interim injunction restraining social media platforms and the makers of Malayalam web series 'Anali' from releasing, promoting, streaming or circulating the show on any over the top platform [ Jollyamma Joseph @ Jolly v JioHotstar Pvt Ltd& ors ]. Judge Reeja R Nair passed the order on August 20 on a plea filed by Jolly, the prime accused in the Koodathayi killings. The Court restrained the web series makers from releasing, publishing, promoting, exhibiting, hosting, reproducing or streaming the web series or any related promotional material to the extent it identifies Jolly with the principal female character and creates an impression that she is the actual perpetrator of the offences in question. The order was passed months after the Kerala High Court had declined to entertain a similar plea filed by Jolly seeking to restrain the show's broadcast. items.title: Arbitrators move Supreme Court after Rajasthan HC cuts their fees citing delay; SC also says "delay is too much"
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently expressed serious concern over the time and costs involved in arbitration proceedings, observing that prolonged hearings defeat the very purpose of choosing arbitration as an alternative to conventional litigation. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observations while hearing appeals filed by arbitral tribunal members in a case arising from the arbitration between HCL Infosystems Limited and Rajasthan power distribution companies including Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited. The arbitral proceedings had commenced in 2020 and 198 hearings had been held with substantial amounts having been paid towards arbitral fees. The process was yet to conclude. The Rajasthan High Court had taken exception to the delay in arbitration and had ordered a 5 percent reduction in the fees charged by arbitrators from April 2025. This prompted the arbitrators to approach the Supreme Court. However, the top court also said the delay was "too long".
